# Seven grid e2e specs each carry their own gridDriver loader

## Context

@neo-fable released this as a claimable grid lane (A2A, 2026-09-19 16:02Z). Measured on `dev@f0a9e0baa5`: seven e2e specs load `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing/gridDriver.mjs` through their own copy of one loader.

## The Problem

Each copy is the same three lines: `Neo.worker.App.loadModule({path})` on the driver URL, a per-file counter appended as `&n=` so every call is a new module URL rather than a cached import, and an `expect(success)` on the reply.
- Six are named `drive(page, action)`: `CellEditingLockedBodies`, `CellEditingPooling`, `CellEditingReprojectionFocus`, `CellEditingRowModel`, `CellEditingStoreActivity`, `CellEditingToggle`.
- The seventh, `LockedRegionEmpties`' `setLocked(page, field, locked)`, adds two query parameters to the same shape.

A change to the loader contract, such as the driver's path, the cache-busting rule or the failure message, has to be made seven times, and a copy that drifts fails only in the spec that carries it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gridCellEditing.mjs` already holds what these specs share (the cell, editor and embodiment reads), "so a change to it reddens both from one place".
- The component tier's `installCancelListener` (`component/grid/CellEditing.spec.mjs`) loads a different module, `cancelListenerDriver.mjs`, and stays out of scope.

## The Fix

One exported `driveGrid(page, action, params)` in `e2e/utils/gridCellEditing.mjs`, with a single counter and the query parameters built from `params`. The seven specs import it, and their local copies and counters go. The net diff is negative.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No e2e spec builds a `gridDriver.mjs` URL itself. `git grep -n "gridDriver.mjs?" test/playwright/e2e` names only the util.
- [ ] The seven specs pass unchanged in what they assert (e2e/grid green), and the diff removes more lines than it adds.

## Out of Scope

The driver module itself, the component tier's cancel-listener loader, and any assertion change.
